answers.question: I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?
answers.answer:
**Not at 53 miles, and not yet.** Feeling good in the first week after a big jump is normal. It does not show that your tendons and calves have caught up.

Your fitness is clearly there. Easy runs held at 139 bpm all week and the 20-miler had even splits. What needs time is the load on your legs, and the calf tightness on Sunday night is an early sign of that.

What you can keep is a higher base. Take next week at about 39 miles, then build back toward the mid-40s in steps of roughly 10% a week. Long runs of 18 to 20 miles are still to come.

If you feel great on an easy day, bank it for the long run and race day instead of adding miles.

new.analysis:
The week showed strong fitness and a loading problem at the same time. Your easy runs sat at 139 bpm and about 9:50 a mile every day, pain stayed at 0/10, sleep averaged 7.5 hours and stress was low. The 20-miler held even splits near 10:02 a mile with only 7 bpm of heart-rate drift.

Every run went over the planned distance, and the rest day became a run.

| Day | Planned | Ran |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mon Sep 7 | rest | 4.0 mi |
| Tue Sep 8 | 6 mi | 7.0 mi |
| Wed Sep 9 | 8 mi, 3 reps | 9.0 mi, 4 reps |
| Thu Sep 10 | 5 mi | 7.0 mi |
| Sat Sep 12 | 4 mi | 6.0 mi |
| Sun Sep 13 | 15 mi | 20.0 mi |
| Total | 38 mi | 53 mi |

Weekly distance went from 37 to 53 miles, and your three-week average was 29. Total effort was 423 against a usual 223. Your lungs and leg muscles adapt faster than your tendons and calves, so how you feel is a poor guide to what you can safely take.

The knee flare in mid-August is a second reason to be careful. It settled after a lighter stretch, and I would rather repeat that pattern than test it. I am reading this week's calf tightness as a cue to ease off, not as a problem.

Your easy-running share was 54%, well under the 80% target. The easy days are not the cause, because they sat at 139 bpm. The cause is the long run, which spent almost three hours in zone 3. Running long runs a little slower is the simplest fix.

Your threshold reps at 7:55 a mile are about 40 seconds faster than the 8:34 pace that gives you 3:45. You do not need extra mileage to chase the goal. You need to reach the start line healthy.

Next week keeps the one quality session at its planned size and shortens the long run. After this step back, long runs return to 18 to 20 miles with marathon-pace segments, then a taper over the last two to three weeks. Keep your two strength sessions on easy days or rest days.
